newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Commonwealth observers happy with Pakistan polls.
newsitem.headline: Commonwealth observers happy with Pakistan polls.

text.p: The leader of a Commonwealth team of observers said that Monday's national and provincial elections in Pakistan had been free and mainly peaceful.
"As the polls closed, it was a picture of largely peaceful elections, a relaxed election day," former Australian prime minister Sir Malcolm Fraser told a news conference.
"Our observers had asked the party workers at different polling booths if they were happy with the arrangements and overwhelmingly the answer to that was 'yes'.
"We are satisfied that those who wished to vote were able to vote, and in the way they wanted to, without any sense of oppression and without any sense of coercion," he said.
Fraser spoke before any results had been announced in the election, which Benazir Bhutto's main rival, former prime minister Nawaz Sharif, was widely expected to win.
